subject: System Design
title: JOINs: Connecting Tables
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on JOINs: Connecting Tables.

hook.text: Users are in one table. Orders are in another. A JOIN connects them to answer: what did each user buy?

buildup.text: JOINs combine rows from two or more tables based on a related column, usually a foreign key.

discovery.text: INNER JOIN returns matching rows. LEFT JOIN includes unmatched rows from the left table too.

twist.text: JOINs across large tables are expensive. Joining million-row tables without indexes can take minutes.

climax.text: JOINs are the superpower of relational databases — and the reason NoSQL databases avoid them entirely.

punchline.text: JOINs connect tables — powerful but expensive at scale.

quiz.question: What does an INNER JOIN return?
options: Only rows that match in both tables
All rows from the left table
